svg.title: Diagram of what USPS pages say about a postal money order. Buying: at a Post Office, from rural carriers or at some contract stations; pay with cash or a debit card with a PIN; checks and credit cards are not accepted; fill in the payee and purchaser and keep the receipt. Cashing: at a Post Office or many banks; do not sign first, bring primary photo ID and sign in front of a USPS employee; no expiry and paid only the printed amount. Checking: the status online needs the serial number, Post Office number and dollar amount; there are no stop payments and no tracing in the mail. Lost or stolen: take the receipt to a Post Office and start a Money Order Inquiry, for which a fee applies; replaced only if not cashed, with up to 30 days to confirm and up to 60 days to investigate; damaged or spoiled ones are replaced at no charge with the money order and its receipt, and without the receipt the FAQ says you can still fill in the inquiry form with the required information. The pages differ on traveler's checks and on refund and replacement timing, and the DMM has separate rules for one payee when the order is completed and several payees when it is cashed.
svg.text: USPS Money Orders
What the USPS pages say
1. Buying
At a Post Office, from rural carriers or
some contract stations. Pay with cash or
a debit card (PIN); no checks or credit
cards. Fill in payee and purchaser; keep
the receipt.
2. Cashing
At a Post Office or many banks. Do not
sign first; bring primary photo ID and
sign in front of a USPS employee. No
expiry; paid only the printed amount.
3. Checking
Status online with the serial number,
Post Office number and amount. No stop
payments and no tracing in the mail.
4. Lost, stolen or damaged
Lost or stolen: take the receipt to a Post
Office and start a Money Order Inquiry (a
fee applies). Replaced only if not cashed:
up to 30 days to confirm, up to 60 to
investigate. Damaged or spoiled: replaced
at no charge with the money order and its
receipt; without the receipt, the FAQ says
you can still fill in the inquiry form with
the required information.
Where the pages differ
Traveler's checks: not accepted (FAQ)
but listed in the DMM. Refund or
replacement timing: 30 days, 10 business
days and 60 days are not reconciled.
Payees: DMM 3.2.4 says one payee when
completing; 3.3.5 covers several when
cashing.
Sources: USPS FAQ 000006987; USPS.com
Sending Money Orders; DMM 509.3; read Nov. 26, 2026
